text.p: Morocco's leading credit firm Eqdom said on Tuesday its 350 million dirham ($36.8 million) three-year fixed rate notes had been fully subscribed.
"The 1,400 notes worth 250,000 dirhams have been subscribed, 99 percent by institutions," said Rachid Tlemcani, director- general of Attijari Finance.
He said the remainder had been acquired by individual shareholders. Attijari and Banque Commerciale du Maroc were responsible for the issue.
Subscription for the notes at an annual fixed rate of 9.5 percent was opened to the public, including foreign institutions, from June 2 to 30.
The notes, with a maturity date of July 1, 2000, can be bought and sold on the Casablanca stock exchange, he said.
Established in Casablanca in 1974 by Morocco's Caisse Centrale de Guarantie and Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Eqdom holds 35 percent of Morocco's market credit share, Upline Securities said.
It showed provisional net profit of 96 million dirhams ($10.32 million) last year from 114.4 million dirhams in 1995.
Listed on the bourse in 1978, Eqdom has capital of 167 million of dirhams.
Among the 47 listed firms, Eqdom was last traded at 952 dirhams, brokers said.
